title: Tauri Production Parity and Electron Retirement

preflight.note: Created during ledger reconciliation before production-parity implementation or Electron removal. Work item 030 established the shared-shell foundation and retirement gate; this item owns satisfying that gate and performing the actual retirement.

acceptance_criteria.text: Inventory every Electron-only API, workflow, lifecycle assumption, packaging path, and operator dependency that must be replaced or explicitly retired.
Prove onboarding and local-service lifecycle parity in Tauri, including startup, authenticated discovery, port conflicts, bounded restart, clean shutdown, and operator recovery.
Prove secure-storage parity for credentials and protected settings without exposing secrets to renderer state, logs, diagnostics, exports, or screenshots.
Prove notifications, deep links, navigation restoration, and single-instance behavior or document platform-specific replacements and limits.
Prove backup, restore, retention, diagnostics, corruption recovery, and data-safety parity without copying the private desktop database to mobile nodes.
Produce reproducible Tauri release artifacts with version metadata, release notes, checksums, update and rollback contracts, and certificate-gated public signing.
Validate a packaged Windows Tauri build through clean-machine or equivalent isolated installation, launch, onboarding, service, cockpit, update, rollback, and uninstall checks.
Record Linux and macOS build, packaging, capability, signing, update, and support posture with tested evidence or explicit bounded limitations.
Remove Electron runtime, packaging, generated renderer assumptions, dependencies, tests, and documentation only after the parity gate is satisfied.
Run post-removal regression, migration, packaged-runtime, rollback, and repository scans proving ForgeLink operates without Electron and can recover from the release transition.
Complete documentation and ledger closeout covering supported platforms, installation, updates, rollback, data safety, known limitations, and remaining risks.
